scouts.angle: tj-playbook: what @tjrobertson52 (TJ Robertson, TJ Digital) teaches, how he formats content, and how TikTok feeds his business
scouts.summary: @tjrobertson52 is TJ Robertson, founder of TJ Digital, a small-business SEO agency he has rebuilt around "AI search". He has 16 to 17 years in marketing and started out as a videographer. Every fact about him here is snippet grade: tiktok.com, tjrobertson.com, YouTube and LinkedIn are all blocked from this container, and I watched no video. His TikTok is a lead-generation arm for a high-ticket service, not an audience business. The snippets show about 17K followers and 112.7K likes, which is modest, and his reach is multiplied by a YouTube channel, LinkedIn, a blog that newsjacks AI-model releases, and at least four podcast guest spots. Recurring topics: AI search optimization (GEO, i.e. getting cited by ChatGPT or Google AI); "parasite SEO" (publishing on Medium, LinkedIn or Reddit to outrank bigger brands); warnings against black-hat tricks such as CTR manipulation; local-SEO location pages; AI repurposing of content; and AI model comparisons. His one concrete, number-free rule on AI citation is that "getting cited is harder than ranking, and the biggest factor is fact density", with topics picked using Peec.ai plus Google Search Console. His positioning is anti-agency transparency ("shows exactly where every dollar goes", "Are agencies scamming you?"). Caption hooks follow a few repeatable forms: a contrarian prediction ("DEAD by 2027 😱"), a pattern the viewer will recognize ("If your competitor suddenly outranks you with worse content..."), a test report ("Tested 20+ new tools - here's what's actually working") and a reaction to news (Gemini 3.1 vs Opus 4.6). Each carries 4 to 5 hashtags mixing broad and niche tags. Three things transfer to Mehudak: fact-dense, citable Hebrew pages built for AI search; newsjacking Israeli tax and VAT changes; and turning one explainer into many formats. His face, his name, the podcast circuit and the sales-call funnel do not transfer, because MISSION.md rules them out. His lead magnet, newsletter and link-in-bio are still unknown and need a runner render.

findings.claim: @tjrobertson52 is TJ Robertson, owner and founder of TJ Digital. It is an agency for small and medium businesses that sells SEO for 'AI-powered platforms like Google, ChatGPT, and TikTok'. He claims 16 years (TikTok bio snippet) or 17 years (LinkedIn headline snippet) in digital marketing, and says he started as a videographer for marketing clients.

The profile snippet shows about 17K followers and 112.7K likes. The capture date is unknown and I did not see the primary page. A small audience that is enough for him is consistent with TikTok feeding a high-ticket service rather than earning from the audience itself.

His core thesis is that 'all search is becoming AI search'. He says he rebuilt his agency around AI, that he uses AI for '90% of my workflow', and that AI lets clients create content '10x faster' at lower cost. The '10x' figure is his marketing claim and nothing backs it.

His concrete AI-citation rule: 'getting cited is harder than ranking', and 'the biggest factor is fact density'. He picks topics likely to be cited by AI using Peec.ai (an AI-visibility tracker) plus Google Search Console. The search engine's summary did not say which of the returned pages holds this; the likeliest are his LinkedIn post on writing website content with AI prompts, or tjrobertson.com.

One video teaches 'parasite SEO': small brands outrank bigger competitors by publishing on Medium, LinkedIn and Reddit (caption: 'This SEO hack lets small brands outrank bigger competitors using Medium, LinkedIn & Reddit'). Only the caption was seen; the steps inside the video are unknown.

He builds trust by positioning against black-hat tactics and against opaque agencies. One video explains CTR manipulation (bots gaming Google, including Maps) and calls it 'a terrible idea'. Another asks 'Are agencies scamming you?'. His agency copy promises to treat 'clients' money as if it were their own' and to show 'exactly where every dollar goes'.

Other advice attributed to him, from a search-engine summary of his profile, so low confidence: most businesses do not need to rebuild their website for AI; on local SEO, Google says not to create a page for every location served, but he recommends doing it anyway, carefully; marketing with AI agents means the team builds systems while AI does the hands-on work. He also covers content repurposing with AI as a podcast guest (Digital Marketing Therapy, Ep 316).

Content format, as far as captions show:
- Hooks follow a few repeatable forms: a contrarian or fear prediction ('Digital marketing will be DEAD by 2027 😱'), a pattern the viewer will recognize ('If your competitor suddenly outranks you with worse content, they might be using bots'), a test report ('Tested 20+ new tools - here's what's actually working'), and a reaction to news ('Gemini 3.1 vs Opus 4.6 — better benchmarks, but does it actually win?').
- Many captions add a retention nudge ('Watch for the exception!', '👇').
- Each carries 4 to 5 hashtags mixing broad tags (#DigitalMarketing, #SEO) with niche ones (#ParasiteSEO, #AIOptimization).
- His LinkedIn snippet claims daily SEO/GEO content on TikTok and YouTube.
- Video length, series structure and whether he is on camera were NOT seen. Talking-head delivery is only my inference from a personal-name brand.

The visible funnel runs from TikTok and short videos to his own agency site. tjrobertson.com is titled 'AI SEO Agency - Rank in AI Search - TJ Digital'. Around it sit a YouTube channel (@TJRobertsonDigital), LinkedIn, and a podcast-guest circuit with at least four appearances: Financial Freedom Podcast, Digital Marketing Therapy Ep 316, NuBeginning, and Primary Position with David Quaid. His link-in-bio target, any lead magnet, any newsletter, and whether he sells through calls or audits are all unknown.

His blog newsjacks AI-vendor releases. A third-party research file on GitHub cites the post https://tjrobertson.com/anthropic-2026-claude-updates/ as a source on Claude's 2026 updates. This shows the post exists and that someone's research agent picked it up. It fits a strategy of fresh, fact-heavy pages that get cited, though that link is inference.

Repo context for applying his AI-citation advice: il-biz-tools pages already carry schema.org JSON-LD. Files include products/il-biz-tools/index.html, vat.html, pcn874.html, registrar-fee.html and the _site/ builds. No products/ directory has an llms.txt. So the missing piece of the fact-density tactic is the content itself, not the markup.

tactics.name: Fact-dense, citable pages for AI search (GEO)
tactics.how_it_works: TJ's rule is that getting cited by an AI answer engine is harder than ranking, and the biggest factor is fact density. The page must be clear, structured, and packed with specific checkable facts, so a model can quote it with confidence.
tactics.evidence: A search-result summary attributes 'getting cited is harder than ranking, and the biggest factor is fact density' to TJ. It is his central agency pitch ('all search is becoming AI search').
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, strongly: faceless, ₪0, honest, and no customer contact. Each il-biz-tools calculator page and the pcn874 validator page would get a short Hebrew block of hard facts: the current VAT rate and its effective date, the osek-patur threshold, registrar fees, and the PCN874 field rules. Each fact links to its gov.il or Tax Authority source and shows a visible 'last verified' date. The JSON-LD already exists (repo), and an llms.txt could be added. Honesty rule: only facts we sourced; no invented statistics to raise 'density'.

tactics.name: Newsjack the regulatory news in our niche
tactics.how_it_works: He publishes fast commentary when something changes in his field. On TikTok it was 'Gemini 3.1 vs Opus 4.6'; on his blog it was a Claude 2026 updates post that other people's research agents then cited. Fresh pages on fresh questions get picked up.
tactics.evidence: The TikTok caption on video 7609111825233251598 (snippet). The blog post tjrobertson.com/anthropic-2026-claude-updates/ is cited in a GitHub research file (github grade).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes. Our news is an Israeli VAT rate change, a threshold update, a new PCN874 or e-invoice (חשבונית ישראל) rule, or a registrar fee change. An agent can watch official sources and, the same day, produce a Hebrew explainer page plus a faceless chart-explainer short that links to the updated calculator. Needs care: publish only after the fact is verified against the primary source, and declare AI use.

tactics.name: Turn one explainer into many formats with AI
tactics.how_it_works: One core piece (a podcast, long video or article) is cut and rewritten by AI into short clips, posts and articles for each platform, stretching one production effort over many channels.
tactics.evidence: His podcast guest episode 'How to Use AI to Repurpose your Content' (Digital Marketing Therapy Ep 316), and a clip of him calling repurposing 'one of my favorite AI strategies' (snippet).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, and it maps onto machinery we already have: one fact-checked Hebrew explainer feeds the web-arm page, the T1 chart-explainer video (Kokoro voice), an optional Telegram bot post, and an ebook chapter source. Not spam, as long as each output is adapted to its platform and not posted as duplicates.

tactics.name: Build trust by calling out black-hat tactics and opaque pricing
tactics.how_it_works: He names shady practices in his own industry (CTR-manipulation bots, agencies that hide where the money goes) and sets his brand against them. That turns honesty into the pitch.
tactics.evidence: Captions on videos 7582743188151078199 ('Here's why that's a terrible idea') and 7504044860782021930 ('Are agencies scamming you?'). Agency copy: 'shows exactly where every dollar goes' (snippet).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, it is the natural voice for Mehudak. For example: 'why you should not trust a VAT calculator that doesn't show its formula'. Then show ours, with open-source code, cited sources, AI use declared, and a free tier that actually works. Do not name or disparage a specific competitor; describe the practice, not a company.

tactics.name: Repeatable caption hooks, with a honesty filter
tactics.how_it_works:
He reuses a few hook forms:
- Contrarian prediction ('X will be DEAD by 2027 😱')
- A pattern the viewer recognizes ('If your competitor suddenly outranks you with worse content...')
- Test report ('Tested 20+ new tools - here's what's actually working')
- Head-to-head comparison
He adds a retention nudge ('Watch for the exception!') and 4 to 5 mixed broad and niche hashtags.
tactics.evidence: Four caption snippets from his TikTok video pages.
tactics.fits_our_constraints:
Partly.
- The 'pattern you recognize' and 'we tested N, here is what works' forms fit if the test is real and reproducible (e.g. 'we checked a PCN874 file against 12 common errors').
- The fear or doom form ('DEAD by 2027 😱') and teaser nudges that the video does not pay off are the engagement bait MISSION.md bans; skip them.
- Hashtag mixing is free and harmless.

tactics.name: Parasite SEO: publish on high-authority third-party platforms
tactics.how_it_works: A small brand borrows the ranking power of Medium, LinkedIn or Reddit by publishing useful posts there that outrank a weak new domain, then links back to its own site.
tactics.evidence: The caption of video 7548494380689149239. The steps shown in the video were not seen.
tactics.fits_our_constraints:
Mixed.
- Medium: a faceless brand publication is allowed and costs ₪0; worth testing with Hebrew articles that link to the calculators.
- LinkedIn: its user agreement expects real-person profiles, so a faceless brand cannot post natively without the owner's identity. No.
- Reddit: self-promotion limits and community rules make it spam-prone, and Hebrew reach there is small. Only genuinely helpful answers with a disclosed affiliation, and only if an agent can do that without the owner talking to anyone. Default: no.

tactics.name: Pick topics by measured AI visibility (Peec.ai plus Search Console)
tactics.how_it_works: Instead of guessing, he uses an AI-visibility tracker (Peec.ai) and Google Search Console query data to pick topics likely to be cited, then writes those pages.
tactics.evidence: A search-result summary attributing the Peec.ai plus GSC workflow to him.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: The Search Console half fits: free, faceless, and an agent can read the GSC API once the site is verified. The Peec.ai half is an unverified paid SaaS whose price I did not check. Under the ₪0 rule, use GSC query data plus Hebrew question lists from our own product analytics until something earns.

tactics.name: Personal-brand podcast guest circuit and service funnel
tactics.how_it_works: He appears as a guest on other people's podcasts (at least four) and posts daily talking-head short videos. All of it drives prospects to a done-for-you agency that sells high-ticket services, where a small follower count is enough.
tactics.evidence: Podcast pages on Apple Podcasts, iHeart, Listen Notes and primaryposition.com, plus the agency site title (snippets).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: No, as a whole. It needs the owner's face, voice and name, live conversations, and sales calls with clients, all excluded by MISSION.md. The transferable lesson: a small, niche, trusted audience can be enough when the offer on the other side is right. For us that offer is a self-serve Pro licence or ebook, not a call.

scouts.summary:
@tjrobertson52 is TJ Robertson, founder of TJ Digital (tjrobertson.com), an agency that sells "AI SEO" / GEO (showing up in ChatGPT and Google AI answers) to small businesses. The search snippets put him at about 17K followers. His TikTok, blog and podcast material makes four teachable points: (1) all search is turning into AI search, and AI recommends businesses it sees mentioned across the web, especially on Reddit; (2) "parasite SEO": publish on Medium, LinkedIn or Reddit, which rank faster than a new domain; (3) check whether anyone searches for a thing before paying for SEO on it; (4) sell on transparency ("shows exactly where every dollar goes", no long-term contracts). Some of his hooks are fear or hype ("Digital marketing will be DEAD by 2027", "Are agencies scamming you?"). We should not copy that style.

I also looked at other TikTok marketing creators. Neil Patel's captions say chatbots cite content that helps someone decide ("Best X for Y", pros and cons, comparison tables) more than "top 10 tips" pieces, and that you should be present on several trusted sites. Small-business lead-magnet videos from @the.leap, and TikTok for Business's own guides, repeat the standard funnel: a free asset that promises to spare the reader pain, then an email list; ads built as hook, then what makes you different, then a call to action.

The one claim I could check on GitHub is the GEO research repo (Aggarwal et al., arXiv 2311.09735). Its README claims GEO "can boost source visibility by up to 40%". Its source code shows what was tested: citing credible sources, adding quotes, statistics, fluency, authoritative tone and simple language. One of those tests adds statistics "even if hypothetical", so part of that measured gain came from made-up numbers, which our honesty rule forbids.

What this means for Mehudak: il-biz-tools already has FAQPage JSON-LD on index, vat and pcn874 (checked in the repo), so the on-page FAQ step is done. The gaps are honest comparison pages and mentions on other sites, which also rules out Reddit posting by bots. Every TikTok claim here is snippet grade. tiktok.com (including oEmbed) and tjrobertson.com both returned "CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403" when I curled them from this container. No video caption or transcript was read first-hand, so the render URLs below are the way to raise the grade.

findings.claim: @tjrobertson52 is TJ Robertson, founder of TJ Digital (tjrobertson.com), which sells AI-SEO / GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) to small and medium businesses. The pitch is that 'all search is becoming AI search', with results in ChatGPT and Google's AI answers. His claimed experience differs between snippets (15, 16 and 17 years). One snippet gives the profile as 17K followers, 140 following and 112.7K likes. The numbers are unverified.

The titles of his indexed TikTok videos show four recurring themes. (a) 'Parasite SEO': small brands outrank bigger ones by publishing on Medium, LinkedIn and Reddit. (b) SEO can waste money if nobody searches for the term, so check demand first. (c) AI-SEO podcast clips about ranking in ChatGPT, Google AI and other LLMs. (d) Fear-and-hype hooks ('Digital marketing will be DEAD by 2027', 'Already using AI for 90% of my workflow', 'Are agencies scamming you?'). Only titles and captions were seen, never the videos.

His own blog makes the AI-visibility thesis concrete in two posts: 'What AI Knows About Your Business in 2026 (and How to Change It)' and 'How to Use Reddit So AI Recommends Your Business (2026)'. The idea is that AI assistants recommend businesses they see discussed on third-party sites, especially Reddit. The posts themselves could not be read here: tjrobertson.com returned a proxy 403.

His positioning for the agency is transparency: it 'treats clients' money as if it were their own', 'shows exactly where every dollar goes', and has no long-term contracts. It is aimed at small businesses that feel burned by opaque agencies.

Neil Patel's TikTok captions (@neilpatel) make two claims: AI chatbots cite decision-stage content ('Best X for Y', bullet points, pros and cons, comparison tables) more than top-of-funnel 'top 10 tips' pieces; and being present across several trusted sites (answering Reddit and Quora questions with researched content, not pitches) makes AI treat you as credible. These are an SEO vendor's claims. No study is cited in the captions.

The search summary gave a statistic, '82% of whether you're recommended in ChatGPT is based on "normal" SEO'. It is not tied to any identifiable source URL. Treat it as folklore until a primary source is found.

The GEO research repo (paper 'GEO: Generative Engine Optimization', Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit, Kalyan, Narasimhan, Deshpande, arXiv:2311.09735) says in its README that GEO 'can boost source visibility by up to 40%' on its own benchmark. The methods it tests are defined in src/geo_functions.py: fluent_optimization_gpt, unique_words_optimization_gpt, authoritative_optimization_mine, more_quotes_mine, citing_credible_sources_mine, simple_language_mine, technical_terms_mine, seo_optimize_mine2 and stats_optimization_mine. The last one's prompt reads 'Add positive, compelling statistics (even if hypothetical)'. So some of the measured gain came from made-up statistics, and that variant fails our honesty rule.

Lead-magnet advice from small-business marketing content on TikTok. Pain-first free assets ('5 biggest mistakes', '7 biggest pitfalls') convert strangers better than promises of big wins. Common formats are ready-to-use templates, a 3-7 day email mini-course, and workbooks. The often-repeated rule that a buyer must see you 12-21 times before buying had no source in anything I saw.

TikTok for Business's own small-business guides recommend: build short video ads as hook, then unique selling point, then call to action; make content that feels native rather than promotional; post consistently; and collect leads in the app with Instant Forms. These are first-party pages, but I saw only snippets.

Our own on-page AI-visibility basics are already in place. products/il-biz-tools/index.html, vat.html and pcn874.html each carry schema.org FAQPage JSON-LD with 3-4 Question/Answer pairs, and there is no llms.txt. The on-page FAQ step is therefore done. What is missing is decision-stage comparison content and honest mentions on other sites.

tactics.name: Honest GEO on-page edits: cite sources, add real statistics, quote authorities, simplify
tactics.how_it_works: Rewrite each product page so an AI answer engine is more likely to quote it. Cite the primary source (Tax Authority or gov.il) for every rule, add real numbers with their source, quote the regulation text, and use plain language. These are the method families the GEO paper benchmarked.

tactics.name: Borrowed-authority publishing (TJ's 'parasite SEO' on Medium, LinkedIn, Reddit)

tactics.fits_our_constraints: Partly. Brand-authored Hebrew articles under Mehudak on Medium or LinkedIn, and dev.to or GitHub for mcp-il-tools, are faceless and ₪0 as long as they are genuinely useful and declare AI use. Paying for placements on other sites, or mass-posting thin pages, is rejected. tactics.fits_our_constraints: The principle fits; the Reddit tactic does not. MISSION forbids spam and customer conversations, so no posting of answers or seeding of threads. The honest version is to get listed where listings are earned and allowed: GitHub READMEs, curated awesome-lists, MCP server registries (for mcp-il-tools), and open-data or tool directories. A Mehudak agent can do this without talking to anyone.

tactics.fits_our_constraints: Strong fit and ₪0. Use it as a gate before each new Hebrew calculator or ebook topic: check Google Search Console impressions for the existing pages once deployed, and use free demand signals the runner can fetch. It matches the colony's kill-gate discipline.

tactics.name: Pain-first lead magnet to email list

tactics.evidence: Search summary of small-business TikTok content and @the.leap. No conversion data was seen. The '12-21 exposures before buying' rule is unsourced.

The free PCN874 validator already works as a lead magnet; a downloadable Hebrew 'common rejection errors' checklist is a cheap addition. Email must be explicit opt-in, since Israeli anti-spam law requires prior consent (background knowledge, grade none; verify). Replies must not require the owner to talk to anyone: auto-replies or a no-reply sender that points to documentation.

tactics.evidence: TikTok for Business guide snippets (first-party but unread).

scouts.angle: hebrew-israel: Hebrew / Israeli sales and marketing on TikTok (Israeli creators teaching שיווק, מכירות, עסקים קטנים, עוסק פטור; what Israeli small-business buyers respond to; WhatsApp-first, trust, the accountant channel)
scouts.summary:
I used all 4 WebSearch calls on the Hebrew/Israeli angle and none on @tjrobertson52 himself, so the sibling scouts will have to cover his page. tiktok.com and timesofisrael.com are blocked from this container: curl to the oEmbed endpoint got a proxy 403, and WebFetch got EGRESS_BLOCKED. Everything about TikTok below therefore comes from search snippets and is snippet grade.

The Hebrew business content the web index can see on TikTok comes from three kinds of accounts:
1. Accountants (רואי חשבון) answering one עוסק פטור question per video: @zoharmamancpa and @nissimhamawi.
2. A creator teaching businesses TikTok marketing in long Hebrew captions packed with keywords: @michael_danilovv.
3. Marketing-service sellers whose call to action is "send me a message". We cannot use that pattern because the owner never talks to customers.

A search for Hebrew sales-closing tips found almost no creators. It mostly returned TikTok's own ads pages. Upload dates decoded from the video IDs run from 2022 to 2025, with two from March 2026, so the Hebrew TikTok index is thin and old.

Two market facts matter for our products, both snippet grade:
- A Times of Israel blog cites Bezeq's State of the Internet Index 2025: 99% of Israelis use WhatsApp and 98% of them daily.
- An accountant's caption describes a new עוסק זעיר status: 30% deemed expenses and no annual report. Our products do not mention it anywhere; I checked the repo.

The repo also shows that il-biz-tools has no WhatsApp share button and no send-to-your-accountant option.

What we can use: an honest "שלח לרואה החשבון בוואטסאפ" (send to your accountant on WhatsApp) share link on results, which the user sends themselves, so there is no customer contact; one-question faceless explainers in the accountant format; accurate long-tail Hebrew captions; and videos timed to rule changes. What we cannot use: the direct-message funnels, and the "secrets agencies won't tell you" hooks.

findings.claim: Israeli accountants are active TikTok creators on עוסק פטור topics. Each video takes a single question as the hook: @zoharmamancpa posted 'האם עוסק פטור יכול להעסיק עובדים❓' with stacked long-tail hashtags (#עוסקפטור #טופס101 #תקרת_עוסק_פטור #אישור_עוסק_פטור #THE_VIKING_ACCOUNTANT); @nissimhamawi posted a long עוסק פטור vs עוסק זעיר explainer. These are the people our buyers already take tax answers from.

The accountant creators use content to generate leads, and the call to action is a personal consultation: @nissimhamawi's caption ends 'מומלץ להתייעץ עם רואה חשבון... תוכל להתייעץ איתי לגבי המסלולים'. The Israeli funnel runs from a free answer to a talk with me. Our brand cannot copy the final step.

According to a creator's caption, a new status called עוסק זעיר exists alongside עוסק פטור: no annual income-tax report required, deemed expenses at 30% of turnover (example: ₪100,000 turnover taxed as ₪70,000 profit), aimed at side income. This is a caption, not a primary source. It must be checked against gov.il or Kol Zchut before we build anything on it.

Our products never mention עוסק זעיר. A grep for 'עוסק זעיר' across products/, skills/ and docs/ returns nothing. The il-biz-tools osek-patur page is titled 'מעקב תקרת עוסק פטור 2026 – כמה נשאר עד ₪122,833?'. If the new status is real, a 'פטור או זעיר?' comparison is an open gap next to a page we already have.

A Times of Israel blog post by Achiya Cohen ('Why WhatsApp-First Is Now Table Stakes for Israeli Small Businesses') cites Bezeq's State of the Internet Index 2025: 99% of Israelis use WhatsApp and 98% of them daily. It argues customers expect businesses to be on WhatsApp.

il-biz-tools has no WhatsApp share, no wa.me link, no navigator.share call and no send-to-accountant option in its source. A grep over its html, js, ts and mjs files, excluding node_modules and _site, finds none. The only mention of accountants is a disclaimer on allocation.html telling users to check with their רואה חשבון.

@michael_danilovv teaches Israeli businesses TikTok marketing in Hebrew. His captions are paragraph-length and repeat search phrases ('שיווק בטיקטוק', 'עסקים בטיקטוק'). Those captions show up in web search results for site:tiktok.com queries, which suggests Hebrew TikTok captions are indexed outside TikTok. One hook uses an us-against-them frame: 'הרבה סוכנויות שיווק לא רוצות שתגדלו'.

The most visible Hebrew 'marketing for your business' TikTok posts from service sellers push viewers to direct messages. @top.social_ (March 2026) says 'שלח הודעה עכשיו ונבנה יחד אסטרטגיה'. A Hebrew search for sales-closing tips returned mostly TikTok for Business ad pages and very few Hebrew sales-technique creators. Both are one-search observations.

A tool-style account aimed at Israeli business owners markets itself with a real workflow question rather than a sales pitch: @tiktok.estimtes asks 'ואיך אתם שולחים הצעות מחיר ללקוחות שלכם? #בעליעסקים #הצעתמחיר'. This is the closest Hebrew analogue I found to a faceless business-tool brand on TikTok.

The Hebrew TikTok business content that web search surfaces is mostly old. Upload dates decoded from the video IDs (the top 32 bits are Unix seconds) are 2022-10 (x2), 2023-01, 2023-10, 2023-12, 2024-12, 2025-01 and 2026-03 (x2). The dates come from the IDs, not from the pages. Web search is a weak way to discover current Hebrew TikTok, so the runner's oEmbed fetches and TikTok's own search are needed to see what is live now.

Global WhatsApp-trust numbers that appear in search results (e.g. '67% higher trust when they can reach a business on WhatsApp', 'NPS 22 points higher') come from messaging-vendor blogs, not Israeli primary data. They should not be quoted in any owner-facing or customer-facing material.

tactics.name: 'שלח לרואה החשבון' WhatsApp share of the result
tactics.how_it_works: On every il-biz-tools result and on the PCN874 validator report, add a button that opens https://wa.me/?text=<URL-encoded Hebrew summary of the result + the page link>. With no phone number in the link, the user picks the recipient themselves, usually their accountant or a partner. Every share puts the tool in front of an accountant without us contacting anyone.
tactics.evidence: Bezeq 2025 figure of 99% of Israelis on WhatsApp (snippet, via a ToI blog). Accountants are the authority our buyers defer to: the Hebrew SERP measurement found accountant blogs ranking for the עוסק פטור and registrar-fee queries (repo, research/measurements/serp/2026-09-07-hebrew-calculators.md), and CPAs are the visible עוסק פטור TikTok creators (snippet). il-biz-tools has no share option today (repo). The claim that wa.me/?text= with no number opens a contact picker is my own knowledge of WhatsApp's documented behaviour, grade none, and needs a test.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, and the best fit on this list. It costs ₪0, is a static-site change, needs no owner face, name or phone number, and involves no customer contact because the user sends the message. The shared text must be the real computed result plus the existing 'not tax advice, check with your accountant' disclaimer, with nothing presented as coming from an accountant.

tactics.name: One-question accountant-format faceless explainers
tactics.how_it_works: Copy the CPA format: the hook is one real question an עוסק פטור searches for ('כמה נשאר לי עד התקרה?', 'פטור או זעיר?'). The answer is on-screen Hebrew text with TTS and a single worked number. The only call to action is the free calculator link, with no 'DM me'. This fits the planned faceless explainer channel (research/faceless-youtube/) and TikTok alike.
tactics.evidence: @zoharmamancpa's question-hook video and @nissimhamawi's עוסק פטור vs זעיר explainer (snippet).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, if every tax figure is checked against a primary source (gov.il, Kol Zchut, the Tax Authority) before publishing, AI use is declared, and the video never presents the brand as an accountant (skills/revenue-il-biz-tools/SKILL.md forbids that). Comments should be off or unanswered, since answering is customer contact. TikTok payouts do not reach Israel (research/tiktok/01), so the aim is traffic to the calculators, not creator income.

tactics.name: Accurate long-tail Hebrew captions and hashtags
tactics.how_it_works: Write paragraph-length Hebrew captions that use the exact search phrases our buyers type (עוסק פטור, תקרת עוסק פטור 2026, דוח 874, טופס 101), plus 3-6 specific hashtags. These captions appear to be indexed by web search engines as well as TikTok search.
tactics.evidence: @michael_danilovv's and @zoharmamancpa's captions came back from site:tiktok.com web searches. That they are indexed is an inference from snippets.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, if each phrase matches what the video actually covers. We should not copy the keyword-stuffed repetition in @michael_danilovv's captions or his 'agencies hide this' framing; the first reads as spam and the second is engagement bait.

tactics.name: Rule-change timing (the new עוסק זעיר status, the annual ceiling update)
tactics.how_it_works: Israeli accountants post when a rule changes. Our equivalent is to ship a calculator or a validator note on the day a change takes effect, such as the yearly תקרת עוסק פטור update or the new עוסק זעיר status. The explainer and the WhatsApp-shareable result then go out while the question is new.
tactics.evidence: @nissimhamawi's caption on עוסק זעיר ('לאחרונה נולד מודל חדש') is snippet grade. Our products do not mention עוסק זעיר at all (repo grep). The osek-patur page already encodes the 2026 ceiling of ₪122,833 (repo).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, if the rule is verified from a primary source first. A wrong tax statement would destroy the trust the product sells. It costs ₪0 and needs no owner contact.

tactics.name: Question prompt to business owners (tool-account style)
tactics.how_it_works: Open a post with a real workflow question aimed at בעלי עסקים ('ואיך אתם שולחים הצעות מחיר ללקוחות שלכם?'), then show the tool doing that job.
tactics.evidence: @tiktok.estimtes (snippet).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Partly. The question hook is honest. But a post built to draw comments creates replies someone would be expected to answer, and the owner cannot answer. Use it only as an on-screen framing device with comments turned off, never as 'comment below and I'll send you…'.

tactics.how_it_works: A free tip or video leads into a direct message or personal consultation, which leads to a sale. This is the dominant pattern among Israeli marketing sellers and accountants on TikTok.
tactics.evidence: @top.social_ and @nissimhamawi captions (snippet).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: No. MISSION.md: the owner never talks to customers. Our replacement for the conversation has to be the self-serve tool, the Pro licence checkout, and the user-initiated WhatsApp share.

tactics.name: Show-don't-tell screen-recording demo of one real calculation
tactics.how_it_works: A 30-60s screen capture of our own tool doing one concrete job, for example the net-salary page on a ₪15,000 gross, the osek-patur ceiling check, or the PCN874 validator catching a comma-split row. Text on screen plus a voiceover, ending with the tool's free URL. No face needed.
tactics.evidence: Vendor playbooks name screen recording with voiceover as a top organic SaaS format and say a ~45s demo of a time-saving feature is the native way to sell software on TikTok.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes on content: it is faceless, honest, original (our own product footage, which clears the FYF originality rule) and ₪0. The same clip works as a YouTube Short, a LinkedIn video and an embed on the tool page. It needs the AI label if the voice is Kokoro. The blocker is posting, which must be manual under a brand account (PUBLISH-9, and the Content Posting API is closed), so it costs owner minutes per post.

tactics.name: One source asset, many platform-native cuts (TJ Robertson's content machine)
tactics.how_it_works: Make one substantive piece, for example the chart-explainer long video or a written guide. Derive short cuts, a text post and a carousel from it, each re-edited for its platform rather than reposted as-is.
tactics.evidence: TJ Robertson is quoted saying repurposing short-form video with AI is the only marketing he does for his agency, and he uses Descript for fast editing.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, if each cut adds edits and value. TikTok's originality rule de-ranks content 'largely repurposed without creative edits', so identical cross-posts are out; the ecc-crosspost skill already says never post identical content. It must stay low-volume and human-reviewed to avoid the mass-produced pattern tiktok/06 rejected. Our chart-explainer pipeline already produces the source asset.

tactics.name: Answer-first hook in the first 3 seconds
tactics.how_it_works: Open with the fact the viewer came for, for example 'Osek patur ceiling 2026: ₪122,833', then show how to check your own case in the tool. The hook is the answer, not a tease.
tactics.evidence: TJ Robertson emphasises nailing the hook in the first 3-5 seconds.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes. It is honest because the hook delivers rather than baits, and it reuses verified numbers from src/config with their source grade. Avoid his 'X is DEAD by 2027' style of fear hook, which is engagement framing that MISSION's no-deceptive-bait rule would reject.

tactics.name: Discover on TikTok, check out off-platform
tactics.how_it_works: No TikTok Shop listing. The bio link and video CTA point to the free tool page, and Pro is bought on Gumroad.
tactics.evidence: Secondary blogs say TikTok Shop does not officially support virtual products (ebooks, courses, PDFs) and advise linking Gumroad, Etsy or Shopify from the bio. The repo says Israel is not on TikTok Shop's country list anyway.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes. This is the only legal checkout path for us, and Gumroad plus il-biz-tools Pro already exist. Unverified: whether a new brand account can show a clickable bio link immediately or only after a follower threshold.

tactics.name: Free tool, then opt-in email, then paid tier (fill the missing rung)
tactics.how_it_works: On each free calculator result, offer an explicit opt-in such as 'email me when the 2027 thresholds or the allocation-number rule change'. Send only factual updates, with Pro mentioned once per mail and a one-click unsubscribe.
tactics.evidence: Free tools for lead generation appear under 'Marketing without Budget' in LisaDziuba/Marketing-for-Engineers (github). il-biz-tools currently has free tools as 'the SEO funnel' and Pro at ₪79 with no email step (repo).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Mostly yes. It is one-way (no conversations), honest and useful, because threshold changes are real events our configs already track. Open risks: a ₪0 sending provider was not researched here, and Israeli anti-spam law requires explicit prior consent (my background knowledge, unverified, grade none), so the checkbox must be unticked by default. Replies would arrive, so an auto-reply pointing to docs is needed to keep the owner out of customer contact.

tactics.name: Be the answer an LLM cites (AI SEO)
tactics.how_it_works: Structured, quotable pages with the number, source and date in plain text, plus the MCP server so assistants call our calculators directly instead of summarising a competitor.
tactics.evidence: TJ Robertson's thesis that search shifts to LLMs and businesses must optimise for them through context engineering.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, and we are already doing the strongest version: mcp-il-tools is free and faceless and needs no posting. The lesson is to keep source/date lines machine-readable on il-biz-tools pages. His two-year timeline is an opinion, not evidence.

tactics.name: Publishing on third-party high-authority sites ('parasite SEO' as pitched)
tactics.how_it_works: Post articles on Medium, LinkedIn or Reddit so they outrank a small site's own pages.
tactics.evidence: TJ Robertson video captioned 'This SEO hack lets small brands outrank bigger competitors using Medium, LinkedIn & Reddit #ParasiteSEO'.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Only the honest subset. One substantive, AI-declared Hebrew guide per real topic, under the Mehudak brand, on LinkedIn or Medium, linking to the free tool, is ordinary publishing. Placing thin content at volume to borrow a site's authority is what search-engine spam policies target (background knowledge; I did not check Google's current policy text, grade none). Reddit self-promotion also invites replies, which means customer contact. Flag as ToS-risky beyond the honest subset.

tactics.name: Multi-account network per audience segment
tactics.how_it_works: Run 5-20 TikTok accounts, one per ICP, use case or geography, posting templated variants.
tactics.evidence: Recommended by a vendor (TokPortal). TikTok's integrity guidelines allow multiple accounts only 'not to deceive others or break the rules' and ban artificial engagement and spam.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: REJECT. It is ToS-risky and spam-shaped, and an agent colony running synchronised templated accounts is the detectable network signature tiktok/06 §3.2 described. MISSION's no-spam rule settles it.

tactics.name: 'Comment KEYWORD and I'll DM you the link'
tactics.how_it_works: The caption asks viewers to comment a word, and an automation or human DMs the product link. This inflates comments and moves the sale into DMs.
tactics.evidence: The owner's reel analysed in the repo used exactly this caption ('Comment "Chatgpt" to get 1K+…'). It is common in the faceless digital-product genre.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: REJECT. It is engagement bait: the comment exists to game ranking, not to add value. It also creates a DM conversation per buyer, which breaks 'owner never talks to customers'. A plain URL on screen and in the bio does the same job honestly.

tactics.name: AI label and originality hygiene on every clip
tactics.how_it_works: Apply TikTok's AIGC label whenever the voice or visuals are synthetic (Kokoro voice counts as realistic audio in my reading). Use only our own footage and charts, not stock compilations. Keep QR codes off screen.
tactics.evidence: TikTok requires labels on realistic AI-generated audio or video and says labelling does not reduce reach for eligible content. Unoriginal or compiled content is ineligible for the For You feed, and creators report 'unoriginal, low quality, or QR content' flags.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, and required. It matches MISSION's declare-AI rule at no reported reach cost. The QR-code point rests only on user reports, so treat it as precautionary.

I used exactly 3 WebSearch calls. I also tried WebFetch on gov.il and kolzchut.org.il; the egress proxy blocked both, so every outside claim below is snippet grade at best.

(1) Hebrew sales teachers. The unknown niche of @edelmanir is now resolved: it is Hebrew sales and negotiation. Three more caption snippets show it (price objections, haggling with telecom companies, 'למכור בלי לשכנע / לאבחן שיטתי'). The IDs decode to 2024-10-16, 2025-01-11 and 2025-01-22, and the earlier-found 7623400135019564309 decodes to 2026-03-31. So this is a live, multi-year Hebrew sales channel. The other Hebrew sales results are older or unusable: @alexgorbachov (2024-03-13, consumer-side), @omerstotsky (2023-09-28, phone sales, keyword-stuffed caption) and @top.social_ (2026-03-31, a 'שלח הודעה עכשיו' DM-funnel agency, which MISSION.md rejects).

(2) עוסק/עסק זעיר. This is NOT a false lead: the track is real. There is a Tax Authority service page titled 'דיווח שנתי מקוצר ותשלום לעסק זעיר', a Kol Zchut concept page 'עסק זעיר (מושג)', and a Capitax article titled 'רפורמת בעל עסק זעיר – ניתוח נתונים תובנות ומסקנות ראשוניות'. Snippets from accountant sites give a 30% automatic deduction with no receipts and a turnover cap of 122,833 ₪ for 2026. Three corrections to the lead:
(a) The 'no annual report' claim from the accountant caption looks wrong. The gov.il title says a SHORTENED annual report ('דיווח שנתי מקוצר').
(b) It is not news. The 2026 search results are crowded with accountant guides and at least one existing calculator (cpa-ea.co.il 'מחשבון עוסק זעיר'). The Capitax 'first data' framing suggests the track has been running for at least a year before 2026 (an inference).
(c) The formal name is 'עסק זעיר' / 'בעל עסק זעיר' (gov.il, Kol Zchut, Capitax). 'עוסק זעיר' is the everyday name accountants use in marketing. It is also a different thing from the repo's VAT-law 'עוסק זעיר לענין סעיף 31(3)': that is a naming collision, not the same thing.
Green Invoice's headline 'מה ההבדל בין עוסק זעיר לעוסק פטור?' implies the track sits BESIDE עוסק פטור rather than replacing it (snippet, from the title only).
Verdict: this is an evergreen SEO/calculator opportunity for il-biz-tools, not newsjacking.

findings.claim: @edelmanir is a Hebrew sales/negotiation educator. The other Hebrew sales results fail the 2025-2026 filter or are anti-patterns: @alexgorbachov 7345753311250779399 'איך לסיים שיחה עם אנשי מכירות מעצבנים #בסטסלר #מכירות' decodes 2024-03-13; @omerstotsky 7283795910423858450 (a keyword-stuffed phone-sales tips caption) decodes 2023-09-28; @top.social_ 7623396885507607816 decodes 2026-03-31 and is a marketing-agency pitch ending 'שלח הודעה עכשיו ונבנה יחד אסטרטגיה' (a DM funnel, targeting car lots by its hashtags).

Across the whole search, Hebrew sales teaching on TikTok still looks thin. One search surfaced one sustained Hebrew sales educator (@edelmanir) and three one-off or dated results. The rest were TikTok's own English-locale ads pages with Hebrew titles.

An income-tax track for micro-businesses exists and the Israel Tax Authority runs a service for it. The gov.il page title is 'דיווח שנתי מקוצר ותשלום לעסק זעיר | רשות המסים בישראל', and Kol Zchut has a concept page titled 'עסק זעיר (מושג)'. So the lead is real, not false.

The 'no annual report' part of the earlier accountant-caption lead is contradicted: the Tax Authority's own service title says 'דיווח שנתי מקוצר' (a shortened annual report), not 'no report'. Any page or video saying 'no annual report' would risk being false. The page body was not fetched (egress blocked), so this rests on the title only.

Deemed-expense rate is 30% of turnover, deducted automatically with no receipts or invoices. The search summary put the turnover cap at 122,833 ₪ for 2026 and gave a worked example: 100,000 ₪ turnover leaves 70,000 ₪ taxable at personal brackets. The track is worth it when real expenses are below 30%, and worse when they are above it. All of this comes from accountant and commercial sites (ucan2, zcpa, vuz, yuvalim, cpa-ea); I could not tell which site gave the 122,833 figure.

The track sits beside עוסק פטור rather than replacing it. Green Invoice's article is titled 'מה ההבדל בין עוסק זעיר לעוסק פטור?', which implies both statuses exist at once. My own reading, not in any snippet: עוסק פטור is a VAT status and עסק זעיר is an income-tax track, so one business could hold both.

Effective date: no snippet stated it. Capitax's title 'רפורמת בעל עסק זעיר – ניתוח נתונים תובנות ומסקנות ראשוניות' implies the reform has run long enough to produce data, so it probably started BEFORE 2026. That makes it not a newsjacking opportunity in September 2026. This is an inference from the title, not a stated date.

Naming: the official sources (gov.il, Kol Zchut, Capitax) say 'עסק זעיר' / 'בעל עסק זעיר'. 'עוסק זעיר' is the everyday name used by accountant and fintech marketing (ucan2, greeninvoice, zcpa, vuz, yuvalim, cpa-ea), and it is what people search. This income-tax track is a DIFFERENT concept from the repo's VAT-law quote 'עוסק זעיר לענין סעיף 31(3) לחוק' (a VAT registration de-minimis in research/colony-sweep/scouts/risk-governance--selling-as-individual.md:132). Do not merge them. The 2026 cap (122,833 ₪) may coincide numerically with the עוסק פטור VAT ceiling, but that is unverified.

The 'פטור או זעיר?' search space is already crowded in 2026. At least 6 accountant or fintech guides target it, and one CPA firm already offers a calculator titled 'מחשבון עוסק זעיר | לחישוב מיסוי קל ונוח'. That is evidence of search demand and of competition, not of an open gap.

The Hebrew copywriting and landing-page search (site:tiktok.com, 'דף נחיתה' OR 'דף מכירה' OR קופירייטינג, לעסקים) returned no Hebrew TikTok copy lessons at all. It returned only TikTok ads pages, Wikipedia and one irrelevant discover page. There is no evidence either way on what Israeli small-business buyers respond to (חשבונית, 'זה רשמי?', Hebrew support, Bit or credit-card trust).

scouts.angle: GAP self-serve-offer-pricing-upgrade: how to build and price the offer, and how to ask a free user to pay, for a ₪79 one-time il-biz-tools Pro licence on Gumroad with no salesperson. I used 3 TikTok searches (Hormozi's offer framework, pricing psychology, freemium conversion), then checked every guarantee and anchor tactic against Gumroad's real mechanics in its open-source code (raw.githubusercontent.com/antiwork/gumroad) and against the repo's pages.
scouts.summary:
TikTok gave a framework but little detail. The lessons that matter came from checking Gumroad's own code.

**What TikTok gave (snippet grade, captions only).**
- @ahormozi's own caption states the Value Equation: "Dream outcome + Perceived Likelihood of Achieving ÷ Time delay + Effort and Sacrifice = Value". It uses + and ÷. The search tool's summary gave a multiplied form instead. Treat the exact form as unverified.
- None of the captions I saw covered Hormozi's guarantee, risk reversal or naming. Those parts of his framework are not evidenced from this search.
- @revelloughlin's caption says most offers fall short on "perceived likelihood of achievement". He fixes it with a "Skillshow - show people how skilled you are, stop telling them" plus testimonial ads "formatted in a way that feels like an authentic conversation". We can use the skillshow. We cannot use the testimonials: we have none, and ads engineered to feel authentic are deceptive.
- The pricing-psychology results are generic: price anchors, charm pricing, crossed-out "original" prices, and lifetime passes for early adopters. Most of it fails MISSION.
- @pm_alliance's caption names the freemium failure: users "binge the content and bounce".

**What Gumroad's code says (github grade, high confidence). These facts decide the tactics.**
- Refund windows are fixed. `RefundPolicy::ALLOWED_REFUND_PERIODS_IN_DAYS` allows only 0, 7, 14, 30 or 183 days, and the default is 30.
- Buyers ask for refunds by replying to the receipt email, which goes to the creator. Gumroad refunds on the creator's behalf only after 30 days with no answer. It also reserves the right to refund within 90 days to prevent chargebacks.
- A refund can only be issued if the seller's balance covers it. Gumroad returns its own fee on a refund but keeps the processing portion.
- If more than 1% of customers dispute, Gumroad forces a 30-day refund policy on the whole account.
- API: `PUT /v2/sales/:id/refund` needs the `refund_sales` or `edit_sales` scope. `PUT /v2/refund_policy` needs `edit_products` and only works if the account-level refund policy is turned on.
- Gumroad's auto-applied discount shows the original price crossed out. This is exactly how a fake "was ₪X" anchor would get produced.
- Adding `?wanted=true` to a product URL opens the payment form directly.

**Consequences for us.**
1. **Don't advertise a money-back guarantee yet.** It is honest only after two things exist: a brand mailbox to receive receipt replies (owner step 8, not done), and a token with `refund_sales` or `edit_sales` so an agent can process refunds. The README documents only `edit_products`. Until then the promise would in practice be kept by Gumroad after 30 days of silence. Receipt replies are also a customer-contact channel that exists whether or not we offer a guarantee.
2. **The best risk reversal for a faceless seller is a try-before-you-buy preview.** The user sees their own logo on a watermarked document before paying. It is the "skillshow", and it needs no customer contact.
3. **The live Pro box never shows the price.** "One-time, no subscription" appears only inside the collapsed "מה נשלח לאן" section. Moving it into the visible text is the cheapest honest fix for the effort-and-sacrifice term.
4. **Ask at the moment of need.** Put one dismissible, non-blocking line next to the print button after a user prints an unbranded document.
5. **pcn874.html should not push Pro,** which has nothing to do with the job the user just did. After a result it should show a plain "why this is free" line pointing to invoice.html#pro.

**Rejected:**
- Invented "was" prices
- Crossed-out prices from a permanent auto-discount
- Comparisons with Morning or iCount subscriptions (different products)
- Early-adopter lifetime passes and countdowns
- Engineered testimonials
- Comment-to-get engagement bait
- Moving any free feature behind the paywall (invoice.html line 111 publicly promises the rest stays free)

findings.claim: @ahormozi's TikTok caption states the Value Equation as 'Dream outcome + Perceived Likelihood of Achieving ÷ Time delay + Effort and Sacrifice = Value'. The search tool summarised it as (Dream Outcome x Likelihood) / (Time Delay x Effort). The caption's operators do not match that summary, so the exact form is unverified.

None of the TikTok captions or snippets this search returned covered Hormozi's guarantee or risk-reversal types, or his naming method. Those parts of his offer framework are NOT evidenced by this research. Anything below about them is my own reasoning.

@revelloughlin's caption says most people fall short on the 'perceived likelihood of achievement' term. He addresses it with a 'Skillshow - show people how skilled you are, stop telling them' and testimonial ads 'formatted in a way that feels like an authentic conversation'. Two other captions from the same creator use comment-to-get: 'Comment "Offer" below for the Google document'.

The Gumroad refund policy model allows exactly these windows: 0 ('No refunds allowed'), 7, 14, 30 and 183 days, each labelled as an 'N-day money back guarantee'. DEFAULT_REFUND_PERIOD_IN_DAYS = 30. Policies are optional per product, are shown on the product page, and are included in card and PayPal disputes.

Buyers request refunds from the creator by replying to the receipt email (reply-to = creator). Gumroad refunds on the creator's behalf only if the creator has not answered for 30 days. It also 'reserves the right to issue refunds within 90 days of purchase, at its discretion, to prevent chargebacks'. Brazil consumers get a 7-day withdrawal even under a no-refunds policy.

If more than 1% of unique customers dispute, Gumroad enforces a refund policy on the whole account. A no-refunds account is moved to a 30-day money-back guarantee, and the seller cannot go back below 7 days while enforcement is active.

Refunds can only be processed if the seller's Gumroad balance covers the amount. On a refund Gumroad returns its own fee but keeps the payment-processing portion. A full refund removes the buyer's access and deletes any rating they gave.

API v2 has PUT /v2/sales/:id/refund, which requires the OAuth scope refund_sales or edit_sales. It also has GET/PUT /v2/refund_policy (seller-level): PUT requires edit_products, accepts refund_period none|7|14|30|183, and fails unless account_level_refund_policy_enabled.

The repo documents the owner's Gumroad token as carrying edit_products (products/il-biz-tools/README.md). Nothing in the repo shows refund_sales or edit_sales. The workflow .github/workflows/gumroad-pro-product.yml sets no refund policy. The brand mailbox is still an undone owner step (research/breadth/REVIEW.md:130).

Gumroad's 'Automatically apply discount code' shows the original price crossed out next to the discounted price on the product page. This is the exact mechanism by which a permanent 'discount' would become a fake anchor.
Adding ?wanted=true to a fixed-price product URL opens Gumroad's payment form directly instead of the product description. It does not work cleanly with pay-what-you-want products.
Pay-what-you-want on Gumroad: the product's Amount is the minimum. With Amount $0, a buyer who chooses to pay must pay at least $0.99. Gumroad takes no fee on free sales.

In its live state the Pro box never shows the price. src/lib/gumroad.js lines 91-93 set the label 'שדרוג ל-Pro' and a note about Gumroad and the licence key. 'תשלום חד-פעמי, בלי מנוי' appears only inside the collapsed <details id="pro-privacy"> at invoice.html line 129. The ₪79 figure lives only in README.md line 34.

The Pro box (invoice.html line 109) sits after the print button (line 103), so the ask follows the value. Line 111 publicly promises that every other tool is free and stays free. #branding-fields (line 137) stays hidden until a licence is active. The invoice FAQ (line 192) has no Pro question.
pcn874.html makes no ask of any kind. It has no Pro, Gumroad or support mention; the page ends with the results section (line 82), the FAQ (line 94) and a disclaimer.
@pm_alliance caption (Collin Mayjack): 'Offering a free trial sounds like a great way to attract customers, but what happens when they binge the content and bounce?'

Pricing-psychology snippets: showing a very expensive item first (a $900 jacket) makes a $160 polo feel reasonable; charm pricing ($19.99); 'price anchoring displays a higher original price next to a discounted price'; an early-adopter lifetime pass that switches to subscription once sold out. The search tool did not attribute these to specific videos.
A snippet from the TikTok #saas tag: 'Low-ticket conversion friction = no adoption', with a recommendation to let product quality convert users. The source video is unattributed.

Israeli distance-selling law likely excludes digital information goods from the 14-day cancellation right. Any Pro guarantee would therefore be voluntary, and the page must not cite consumer-protection law as its basis. This comes from the repo's consumer-protection scout, which relied on a secondary source.

tactics.name: Value-equation rewrite of the visible Pro box (price, one-time, instant, what is included)
tactics.how_it_works: Map each term to a true, checkable sentence in the box's visible text, not inside collapsed <details>. Dream outcome: 'your logo and brand colour on every receipt you print'. Time delay: the key comes in the Gumroad receipt and branding switches on as soon as it is pasted. Effort and sacrifice: '₪79, one payment, no subscription, no account, your data stays in your browser'. The price shown must be read back from Gumroad by gumroad-pro-product.yml and written into src/config/site.json, never hand-typed, so the page cannot show a number Gumroad does not charge.
tactics.evidence: The Hormozi caption names the four terms (snippet). Repo: the live note at gumroad.js:91-93 shows no price, and 'חד-פעמי' is hidden in the #pro-privacy details at invoice.html:129.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes. Files: invoice.html lines 109-113 (pro box heading and paragraph), src/lib/gumroad.js lines 91-93 (label and note), src/config/site.json (a price field written by the product job). Wording principle: state the deliverable, never an outcome we cannot evidence ('look professional' is fine; 'win more clients' is not). Needs a page test asserting the displayed price equals the configured one.

tactics.name: Try-before-buy preview as the no-contact risk reversal (the Skillshow)
tactics.how_it_works: Let a free user upload a logo and pick a colour in #branding-fields and see the branded document on screen, with a visible 'תצוגה מקדימה – Pro' watermark on print until a licence is active. Likelihood of achievement is proved by the user's own document, not by testimonials, and the doubt is removed before payment, so no refund conversation is needed.
tactics.evidence: @revelloughlin caption: 'Skillshow - show people how skilled you are, stop telling them' (snippet). Repo: #branding-fields at invoice.html:137 stays hidden until licensed.
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, and it is the best fit found: it needs no customer contact, no testimonials and no promises. Files: invoice.html #branding-fields (line 137) and assets/page-invoice.js, with a test that print output carries the watermark when unlicensed. Wording: call it a preview plainly. Client-side gating is already acknowledged as bypassable in the README, so the preview does not change the threat model.

tactics.name: Moment-of-need ask next to the print button
tactics.how_it_works: After a user prints or saves a PDF of an unbranded document, show one dismissible line beside #print, e.g. 'המסמך הודפס בלי לוגו. Pro מוסיף לוגו וצבע – ₪79, חד-פעמי', linking to #pro. It never blocks printing and never uses a modal or timer. Show it at most once per session; the dismissal is remembered in localStorage wrapped in try/catch.
tactics.evidence: @pm_alliance 'binge and bounce' caption (snippet). Freemium advice seen on TikTok is to convert at the point where the paid feature is missing (snippet, low).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Yes, if it is non-blocking, factual and shown once. File: invoice.html around line 103 (the actions div) plus assets/page-invoice.js. Reject guilt or shame copy ('still using a plain receipt?') and any nag that repeats.

tactics.name: Money-back guarantee through Gumroad's refund policy (CONDITIONAL; do not advertise yet)
tactics.how_it_works: Set a window Gumroad supports (7, 14 or 30 days) via PUT /v2/refund_policy (edit_products scope, and only if the account-level policy is enabled) or via the product setting. Quote Gumroad's own title text exactly in the pro box and the FAQ. Process refunds by agent through PUT /v2/sales/:id/refund.
tactics.evidence: refund_policy.rb (windows 0/7/14/30/183, default 30); help articles 190, 51 and 47 (refund requests arrive as receipt replies to the creator; Gumroad steps in after 30 days of silence; refunds need a balance that covers them); refund_policies_controller.rb and sales_controller.rb (scopes).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: Not yet. It becomes honest only when (a) a brand mailbox receives receipt replies (owner step 8 is not done) and (b) the token has refund_sales or edit_sales so an agent can process a refund without the owner. Until then the promise would be kept by Gumroad after 30 days of silence, which does not match the words on the page. Never write 'no questions asked', never promise results, and never cite Israeli consumer-protection law (digital goods are likely excluded). Files, when ready: the pro box on invoice.html and a new FAQ entry at invoice.html:192, mirrored in the FAQPage JSON-LD at line 15.

tactics.name: Honest price display instead of anchoring
tactics.how_it_works: Show one real price once. Charm pricing (₪79) is neutral and fine. No crossed-out 'original' price. Use Gumroad's auto-applied discount (which shows the original price crossed out) only for a real, dated promotion where the full price is actually charged before and after it, and not at launch. Do not compare with Morning or iCount annual plans: they are full invoicing systems, so the comparison implies an equivalence that is false.
tactics.evidence: Anchoring and crossed-out price advice on TikTok (snippet). Gumroad's auto-apply discount renders the crossed-out original (github).
tactics.fits_our_constraints: The anchoring tactic as taught fails MISSION; an invented 'was ₪199' is rejected. The honest residue is 'state the true price plainly', which is already covered by the value-equation rewrite. The rule belongs in the product job: never set an automatically applied offer code without an end date.

tactics.how_it_works: Point the Pro button at productUrl + '?wanted=true' so Gumroad opens the payment form directly and skips one page.
tactics.evidence: Gumroad help article 144 (github). Snippet: 'Low-ticket conversion friction = no adoption' (low).
